semanticReview.method: Seguimiento R33: relectura completa del artículo, reapertura de la revisión anterior, búsquedas distintas en fuentes institucionales/académicas gratuitas e inspección de los pasajes listados. Se conserva pendiente cuando no hay cobertura de todas las afirmaciones materiales.
findings: わたくし is a formal first-person expression more formal than わたし. The official guidance calls it a term for formal occasions; CEJC’s small five-token sample shows it can also be used in casual familiar conversation.

It is used primarily in professional, careful or ceremonial settings and signals social distance. Historical guidance supports formal occasions; CEJC shows five familiar casual uses and no distancing, so the article’s broad current restriction conflicts with observed primary corpus data.
The article’s わたくし/particles examples are ordinary and correctly glossed. No source-located examples from the cited materials match these examples.
First-person pronouns may be omitted when context identifies the speaker. The official report notes frequent non-use of personal pronouns generally; it does not isolate first-person omission here.
わたくし is not gender-marked. The older guidance proposes it as a standard formal form across genders; it does not establish contemporary identity-related usage.
